source_name: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije (TZS) – Slovenian Chamber of Commerce (retail/trade)
why_relevant: Represents merchants — the acceptance side of payments. Positions on interchange fees, surcharging, card acceptance costs, cash-handling obligations and the cash-accessibility bill are the counterweight to ZBS positions; its legislation section tracks trade-law deadlines.

source_name: AmCham Slovenia – Finance Committee
why_relevant: Cross-industry advocacy committee focused on the tax and financial environment; AmCham runs formal advocacy positions and its member list points to international banks, payment firms and advisers active in SI. Bilingual (en/sl) output eases monitoring.

source_name: Digitalna koalicija Slovenije – Delovne skupine (working groups)
why_relevant: National multi-stakeholder digital coalition whose working groups (incl. a blockchain working group uniting Blockchain Think Tank Slovenije, Blockchain Alliance Europe and Bitcoin društvo Slovenije) coordinate industry input into digital/crypto legislation. Strong pointer into the SI fintech self-organisation layer.

source_name: Bitcoin društvo Slovenije (Bitcoin Association of Slovenia)
why_relevant: Self-declared purpose includes actively participating in shaping national and EU legislation; publicly opposed the Ministry of Finance's proposed 25% crypto gains tax (2025), which was subsequently shelved. Useful early-warning source for SI crypto-asset regulation and its political viability.

source_name: Državni zbor / e-Demokracija consultation trail carrying association submissions (pointer to who responded)
why_relevant: Parliamentary and public-consultation records name the interested-public bodies that filed comments (associations such as ZBS, VZMD, GZS, TZS) and carry their submitted texts — the way to catch association positions that never appear on the association's own site. VZMD's repeated submissions on bank-related bills are a documented example.

source_name: VZMD – Vseslovensko združenje malih delničarjev/deležnikov (All-Slovenian Shareholders' Association)
why_relevant: A persistently active self-organised stakeholder association in Slovenian banking legislation (notably the bail-in / qualified bank liabilities compensation laws). Publishes its own submissions to Parliament, giving visibility into consultation timing and the opposing side of bank-sector positions.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil (enarocanje.si) — Uradni list RS
why_relevant: Slovenia's statutory national publication portal for all contract notices (obvestila o naročilu), corrections, award notices and contract amendments, operated by Javno podjetje Uradni list RS d.o.o. All Slovenian public buyers — including Banka Slovenije, ministries, UJP, municipalities and state-owned companies — must publish here, so compliance-driven banking/payment/supervisory-IT projects surface with scope, estimated value and hard submission deadlines months before any public announcement. Bank of Slovenia's own pages point to this portal as the place its procurement documentation is published.

source_name: e-JN — Elektronsko javno naročanje (ejn.gov.si)
why_relevant: The state e-procurement transaction system (Ministrstvo za javno upravo / Direktorat za javno naročanje) where tender documentation is issued and bids are submitted electronically. Its 'Aktualna javna naročila' listing exposes live procedures with deadlines; it is the operational counterpart to the enarocanje.si notice layer and often holds the actual specification documents for supervisory-reporting and AML tooling.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ Supplement)
why_relevant: All Slovenian above-threshold contracts (services threshold in the ~EUR 140k range for central authorities) must be published in TED in parallel with the national portal. TED gives structured, multilingual, CPV/NUTS-filterable coverage of SI banking-services and supervisory-IT tenders, plus award notices revealing incumbent vendors and contract values. Already surfaced a Slovenian banking-services procurement (Aerodrom Ljubljana/Brnik).

source_name: TED Search API / TED Open Data (docs.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Authentication-free machine interface to TED notices (expert queries, bulk XML download, SPARQL endpoint, eForms SDK). This is the sustainable collection mechanism for the whole EU-threshold layer of the Slovenian public-buyer route — enabling continuous monitoring of SI banking/payments/supervisory-IT tenders with deadlines and award data.

source_name: OPSI — Odprti podatki Slovenije: 'Aktualna javna naročila v informacijskem sistemu e-JN' dataset
why_relevant: Machine-readable open-data mirror of the live e-JN tender list published by the Ministry of Public Administration — the cleanest structured feed for current Slovenian procurements without scraping JSF pages.

source_name: OPSI — Zbirka letnih statističnih poročil o oddanih javnih naročilih
why_relevant: Annual statutory statistics on awarded public contracts (prepared under ZJN-3 by the Ministry and approved by Government). Gives multi-year baselines for how much the Slovenian public sector spends on financial/banking services and IT, useful for sizing the addressable public-buyer segment and spotting trend breaks.

source_name: Direktorat za javno naročanje (MJU) — poročila, analize, usmeritve
why_relevant: The policy owner of the Slovenian procurement system. Its guidance, circulars and analyses tell you how buyers are being told to structure financial-services and IT tenders (e.g. joint/central procurement, framework agreements), which shapes the shape and timing of banking/payments tenders. Also an authoritative pointer to all system components (e-JN, portal, ESPD, e-Dosje).

source_name: Državna revizijska komisija (DKOM) — odločitve / iskalnik
why_relevant: Independent review body deciding bid-protest disputes (zahtevek za revizijo). Its published decisions expose tender requirements, competitor arguments, disqualification grounds and pricing disputes in banking-services and IT procurements in far more detail than the notice itself — and reveal which awards are delayed, which shifts real delivery dates.

source_name: ERAR (KPK) — public-money transaction transparency application
why_relevant: Anti-Corruption Commission application (successor to Supervizor, rebuilt 2023-2025) exposing actual payment flows from public bodies and state/municipally owned companies to suppliers under Arts. 75a/75b ZIntPK. Lets you verify who actually gets paid for banking, payment-processing and compliance-software work after award, including contracts below publication thresholds — i.e. the vendor landscape a tender notice alone will not show.

source_name: UJP — Uprava RS za javna plačila: JN Plačila / e-Plačila
why_relevant: UJP is the state payments administration and itself a public buyer and operator of payment rails for the whole budget-user population. The JN Plačila portal (transaction reporting + contract publication for procurement payments) and UJP e-Plačila (card, mobile — VALÚ Moneta, mBills — and NLB Klik acceptance) define the public-sector payments stack; changes and related tenders are direct commercial signals for payment vendors.

source_name: Mestna občina Ljubljana — Služba za javna naročila (buyer-side publication)
why_relevant: Representative large municipal buyer profile. Municipalities procure banking services (account operation, cash handling, POS acceptance, loans) and are a recurring, below-EU-threshold segment invisible on TED. Ljubljana is the template for building a buyer-profile watchlist across the largest Slovenian municipalities and public utilities.

source_name: PISRS — Zakon o javnem naročanju (ZJN-3)
why_relevant: The governing procurement statute, including the rule that banking and other financial services are valued on fees, commissions and interest — which determines whether a banking-services contract crosses the EU threshold and therefore whether it appears on TED at all. Needed to interpret thresholds, exemptions and publication duties correctly.

source_name: PISRS — Zakon o plačilnih in javnofinančnih storitvah (ZPJS)
why_relevant: Defines how budget users (proračunski uporabniki) obtain payment and public-finance services — i.e. the legal frame that decides whether a public body buys payment services on the market via tender or receives them from UJP/Banka Slovenije. Directly determines the size of the addressable public-sector payments tender market.

source_name: javni-razpisi.si — commercial tender aggregator (SI/HR/RS region)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator of Slovenian and regional tender notices with its own categorisation and alerting. Useful as a redundancy/cross-check layer against enarocanje.si and to catch notices whose CPV coding is wrong, but not authoritative and likely subscription-gated for detail.

source_name: S-PROCUREMENT (s-procurement.si) — e-procurement/e-auction vendor platform
why_relevant: Private e-procurement/e-sourcing platform used by Slovenian buyers alongside the state system. Some public and state-owned buyers run their sourcing here, so its public notice listing can surface procedures (and vendor references) not obvious on the state portal; also a competitor/partner signal in the procurement-tech layer.

source_name: e-Justice / gov.si — 'Na katerih spletiščih se objavijo uradna obvestila?' (SI official publication map)
why_relevant: Authoritative EU/national map of which Slovenian websites carry which mandatory official announcements, including procurement. Useful to guarantee the source inventory for this cell has no legally-required publication channel missing (Uradni list RS, portal javnih naročil, AJPES, etc.).

source_name: EU Public Procurement portal (op.europa.eu) — procurement detail records
why_relevant: Publications Office front-end presenting individual procurement records (including Slovenian banking-services procurements) in a stable, citable form; complements TED notices with consolidated per-procedure views useful for evidencing award histories.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Investor Relations - Press Releases (Bankart Vynamic Transaction Middleware win)
why_relevant: Vendor IR newsroom carrying the May 2024 announcement that Bankart (the processor owned by NLB and serving ~20 banks in 6 SEE countries) is replacing its legacy BASE24 platform with Vynamic Transaction Middleware. Vendor win announcements are the only public dating of core payment-platform migration projects at Slovenian private banks, and such migrations are directly driven by instant-payments/PSD2/DORA resilience deadlines.

source_name: Temenos Success Stories / Customer References (Nova Ljubljanska Banka)
why_relevant: Core-banking vendor reference page documenting NLB's T24/Transact deployment and later retail migration. Establishes which core platform the largest SI bank runs, which in turn determines the vendor channel through which regulatory change (IFRS, PSD2, DORA, instant payments) is delivered.

source_name: Iliad Solutions - News (Bankart multi-year payment testing deal)
why_relevant: Payment-testing vendor announced a multi-year deal with Bankart (2025). Test-tooling contracts are a leading indicator of scheme/regulatory migration programmes (instant payments mandate, ISO 20022, card scheme mandates) at the Slovenian processor.

source_name: Halcom d.d. - corporate news / banking solutions (halcom.com, halcom.si)
why_relevant: Ljubljana-headquartered digital-banking and payments vendor present in 60+ banks and 2 central banks/clearing houses across EMEA; historically built the first e-bank for NLB and co-implemented SEPA/euro payment reforms. Its Slovenian-language news and product pages date regulatory-driven projects (SEPA, instant payments, PSD2 SCA, qualified certificates/eIDAS) inside private SI banks.
